# Resource port

Create/Update/Delete a VLAN (such as node1:e0a-100) or LAG (ifgrp, such as node2:a0a).

### Related ONTAP commands

```commandline
* network ifgrp create
* network ifgrp modify
* network ifgrp delete
* network vlan create
* network vlan modify
* network vlan delete
```

## Supported Platforms

- On-perm ONTAP system 9.6 or higher
- Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netapp-ontap_port" "lag" {
  cx_profile_name = "cluster4"

  broadcast_domain = {
    ipspace = "Default"
    name    = "Default"
  }

  node = {
    name = "netapp_single-01"
  }

  type = "lag"
  lag = {
    distribution_policy = "mac"
    member_ports = [
      "e0b",
      "e0c",
    ]
    mode = "singlemode"
  }
}
```

```terraform
resource "netapp-ontap_port" "vlan" {
  cx_profile_name = "cluster4"

  broadcast_domain = {
    ipspace = "tf_test"
    name    = "tf_test_data_svm02"
  }

  node = {
    name = "netapp_single-01"
  }

  type = "vlan"
  vlan = {
    base_port = "e0a"
    tag       = 300
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->

## Argument Reference

### Required

- `cx_profile_name` (String) Connection profile name
- `node` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--node))
- `type` (String) Type of physical or virtual port

### Optional

- `broadcast_domain` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--broadcast_domain))
- `enabled` (Bool) Port enabled
- `lag` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--lag))
- `vlan` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vlan))

### Read-Only

- `name` (String) Portname, such as e0a, e1b-100 (VLAN on Ethernet), a0c (LAG/ifgrp), a0d-200 (VLAN on LAG/ifgrp), e0a.pv1 (p-VLAN, in select environments only)
- `reachability` (String) Reachability status of the port
- `state` (String) Operational state of the port
- `id` (String) Port UUID

<a id="nestedatt--node"></a>

### Nested Schema for `node`

Optional:

- `name` (String) Name of the node on which the port is located
- `id` (String) Node UUID

<a id="nestedatt--broadcast_domain"></a>

### Nested Schema for `broadcast_domain`

Optional:

- `ipspace` (String) Name of the broadcast domain's IPspace
- `name` (String) Name of the broadcast domain, scoped to its IPspace
- `id` (String) Broadcast domain UUID

<a id="nestedatt--lag"></a>

### Nested Schema for `lag`

Required:

- `distribution_policy` (String) Policy for mapping flows to ports for outbound packets through a LAG (ifgrp)
- `member_ports` (Set of String) Array of ports belonging to the LAG, regardless of their state
- `mode` (String) Determines how the ports interact with the switch

Read-Only:

- `active_ports` (Set of String) Active ports of a LAG (ifgrp)

<a id="nestedatt--vlan"></a>

### Nested Schema for `vlan`

Required:

- `base_port` (String) VLAN base port
- `tag` (Number) VLAN ID

## Import

This Resource supports import, which allows you to import existing ethernet port into the state of this resoruce.
Import require a unique ID composed of the cx_profile_name and port name, separated by a comma.
id = `cx_profile_name`,`name`

### Terraform Import

For example

```shell
 terraform import netapp-ontap_port.example cluster4,e0a-300
```

!> The terraform import CLI command can only import resources into the state. Importing via the CLI does not generate configuration. If you want to generate the accompanying configuration for imported resources, use the import block instead.

### Terraform Import Block

This requires Terraform 1.5 or higher, and will auto create the configuration for you

First create the block

```terraform
import {
  to = netapp-ontap_port.vlan_import
  id = "cluster4,e0a-300"
}
```

Next run, this will auto create the configuration for you

```shell
terraform plan -generate-config-out=generated.tf
```

This will generate a file called generated.tf, which will contain the configuration for the imported resource

```terraform
# __generated__ by Terraform
# Please review these resources and move them into your main configuration files.
# __generated__ by Terraform from "cluster4,e0a-300"
resource "netapp-ontap_port" "vlan_import" {
  cx_profile_name = "cluster4"
  type            = "vlan"
  node = {
    name = "netapp_single-01"
  }
  vlan = {
    base_port = "e0a"
    tag       = 300
  }
}
```
